top.headline: Justice Department Subpoenas California Election Workers in Noncitizen Voter Dispute
top.blurb: The Justice Department subpoenaed employees of the Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder's office, ordering at least two to testify November 4, a day after a federal judge rejected DOJ's demand that the county set aside ballots from 20,000 voters it flagged as likely noncitizens. Judge David O. Carter doubted the list's reliability and warned 'these threats must stop'; DOJ is appealing to the 9th Circuit.

top.headline: Alaska's Pivotal Senate Race Roiled by Report of a Democratic Plot to Recruit a Spoiler Candidate
top.blurb: A New York Times report alleges Democratic operatives, including aides to Mary Peltola's campaign, tried to recruit a second candidate named Dan Sullivan to split votes from the Republican incumbent in Alaska's toss-up Senate race. Peltola's campaign denies involvement; Gov. Mike Dunleavy ordered a state investigation, and DOJ amended its existing election lawsuit to cite the report.

top.headline: How ICE Operates in the Shadows of the Civil Immigration System
top.blurb: Reporting with The Marshall Project traces Pedro Vasquez Perdomo's arrest by masked ICE agents at a Pasadena bus stop and his transfer to a downtown LA processing site so crowded lawyers called it a 'black hole.' Because immigration detention is civil, not criminal, detainees often get no lawyer and little notice before being moved — a gap a federal judge has only partly curbed since.

top.headline: Arunachal Police Seek Search Warrant Against Journalist Tongam Rina Over Anti-Dam Protest Violence
top.blurb: Arunachal Pradesh Police asked a court for search warrants against Tongam Rina, deputy editor of The Arunachal Times, alongside an activist, a youth leader and a lawyer, after protests against the 12,500-megawatt Upper Siang dam turned violent in Pasighat. Press bodies called including Rina's name a serious threat to press freedom; 69 people have been arrested.

top.headline: Madhya Pradesh Spent ₹230 Crore Promoting a ₹30-Lakh-Crore Investment Summit That Yielded No Signed MoUs
top.blurb: Chief Minister Mohan Yadav touted ₹30.77 lakh crore in MoUs at Bhopal's 2025 Global Investors Summit — over seven times the state's annual budget — but the government later told the assembly no MoU had been signed since 2020, recasting the deals as mere 'investment intent.' The largest single entry, ₹3 lakh crore, came from a company with just ₹10,556 in the bank.

top.headline: Election Commission Extends SIR Claims Deadline in Delhi and Maharashtra After Mass Deletions
top.blurb: The EC reopened Maharashtra's claims window, which had closed October 26, until November 13, and pushed back processing deadlines in four more states, after a Supreme Court suggestion. The extension follows the deletion of 47.7 lakh names — a third of the electorate — from Delhi's draft voter list during the special intensive revision.

top.headline: Israel Election Ends With No Clear Winner as Netanyahu's Bloc Falls Short of a Majority
top.blurb: With the vote count complete, Netanyahu's right-wing bloc leads but lacks the seats to form a government outright, leaving Israel's first election since the October 7 attacks unresolved. President Isaac Herzog is expected to consult the parties before naming someone to try forming a coalition, a process that could take weeks or months.

top.headline: 'Arab Voice Doesn't Count': Jewish Israeli Blocs Rule Out Governing With Palestinian Parties
top.blurb: About 80% of eligible Palestinian citizens of Israel voted, a surge that gave the Ra'am and Joint List alliances a combined 19 seats — enough that the anti-Netanyahu bloc needs them for a majority. But Bennett, Lapid and Lieberman have all ruled out governing with Palestinian parties, and Likud has asked Shin Bet to probe the turnout for 'foreign interference.'

top.headline: Drone Strikes on a Darfur Market Kill More Than 100 in Sudan's Civil War
top.blurb: Drone strikes on a crowded market in Nyala, the paramilitary RSF's de facto capital in South Darfur, killed more than 100 people and wounded 113, the rights group Emergency Lawyers said, with most of the dead reported to be women and children. The UN says drone strikes are now the leading cause of civilian death in Sudan's four-year civil war.

top.headline: Patrick Stewart, Star Trek's Captain Picard and X-Men's Professor X, Dies at 86
top.blurb: Stewart died at his Los Angeles home, with a statement describing a 'brief and poignant journey' with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia. He joined the Royal Shakespeare Company in 1966, played Captain Jean-Luc Picard across seven seasons of Star Trek: The Next Generation and its sequel series, and starred as Professor Charles Xavier in the X-Men films from 2000 onward.

top.headline: Netflix's New 'Pride and Prejudice' Trailer Pairs Emma Corrin With Jack Lowden's Darcy
top.blurb: Netflix released the trailer for its new Pride and Prejudice adaptation, with Emma Corrin as Elizabeth Bennet and Jack Lowden as Mr. Darcy, alongside Olivia Colman and Rufus Sewell. The six-episode series premieres December 3.

bengal.headline: Abhishek Banerjee Questions Transparency of Chorbagan Stampede Probe
bengal.blurb: TMC leader Abhishek Banerjee demanded the arrest of three BJP functionaries linked to the Chorbagan stampede that killed 19 people, accusing police of acting on the BJP-led state government's behalf.

bengal.headline: Suvendu Adhikari Proposes Bengal's Second AIIMS for Raiganj
bengal.blurb: Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari proposed building Bengal's second AIIMS at Dwipnagar in Raiganj, offering about 180 acres, and announced a new cancer care hospital for Jalpaiguri.

bengal.headline: Kolkata and Howrah Civic Polls Likely Pushed to December
bengal.blurb: The West Bengal State Election Commission began preparations for Kolkata and Howrah municipal elections, with about 22,613 polling staff needed for Kolkata alone, as officials weigh dropping the NOTA option.

travel.headline: A Philippine Village Rebuilt Its Flood Defenses From Bamboo, Oyster Shells and Coconut Husks
travel.blurb: After a concrete breakwater failed, the fishing village of Pamarawan on Manila Bay built 14 hectares of bamboo cribs and shell-filled husk nets to tame storm waves and regrow mangroves and oyster reefs; residents say they haven't flooded in nearly two years.

happy.headline: As Winnie-the-Pooh Turns 100, the Original Stuffed Toys Stay Put in New York — With the Queen's Blessing
happy.blurb: For the centenary of A.A. Milne's books, biographer Gyles Brandreth asked the New York Public Library, on behalf of Queen Camilla, to loan Christopher Robin's original Pooh, Piglet, Eeyore, Kanga and Tigger to Buckingham Palace. The library said no — 'they are staying put' — so the queen instead sent a replica of Roo, the toy kangaroo lost in an English orchard in the 1930s, to join the display.

tech_top.headline: Binance Pauses Withdrawals as Hackers Suspected of Draining Billions From Its Hot Wallets
tech_top.pm_note: Tether and Circle could freeze over $2 billion of the stolen funds within hours — a reminder that stablecoin issuers, not exchanges, are often the real circuit breaker when crypto custody fails.
tech_top.blurb: Binance confirmed a security incident and suspended withdrawals after users reported funds draining from its wallets, with crypto trackers estimating $2 billion to $5.7 billion taken. Tether froze about $1.56 billion and Circle froze $800 million tied to the hack; the attackers remain unidentified.

tech_top.headline: Senators Demand Meta Explain 'Pervert Glasses' Footage Found After a 404 Media Investigation
tech_top.pm_note: A wearable camera turns every user into a potential publisher of footage of bystanders who never consented — a liability model current privacy policies weren't built to cover.
tech_top.blurb: 404 Media found Instagram accounts with hundreds of thousands of followers posting Ray-Ban Meta glasses footage of men soliciting sex workers at massage parlors. Senators Wyden and Markey are now asking Meta what safeguards exist against nonconsensual recording and whether such footage is used, with human reviewers, to train its AI.

tech_top.headline: Waymo Will Build Its Next Robotaxi With Toyota, Aiming at Japan and the UK
tech_top.pm_note: Partnering with an established automaker to localize for right-hand-drive markets is a build-vs-partner call every hardware-dependent AI product eventually faces when it goes global.
tech_top.blurb: Waymo and Toyota will integrate Waymo's self-driving system into Toyota bZ4X electric vehicles built at Toyota's Takaoka factory, targeting Japan first and other right-hand-drive markets like the UK next. The companies also plan to explore bringing the technology to personally owned Toyota vehicles.

tech_more.headline: GM to Pay $220 Million After Selling Drivers' Location and Behavior Data to Insurers
tech_more.blurb: GM settled with 36 states over claims it sold driving data to brokers who passed it to insurers, and must now get drivers' explicit consent before collecting or sharing it.

tech_101.text: A cryptocurrency wallet connected to the internet for quick trading, as opposed to a 'cold' wallet kept offline. Hot wallets are convenient but are the ones hackers can actually reach, which is why exchanges like Binance keep most customer funds elsewhere.

science.headline: A New Catalytic Process Recycles Silicone Waste Into Reusable Building Blocks at Up to 99% Yield
science.blurb: Chemists at the Technical University of Berlin, led by Martin Oestreich, broke down silicone waste from everyday products into dimethyldichlorosilane, a building block for new silicone, using a silylium-ion catalyst. Yields reached 99% for single products and 86% for a mixed batch, offering a path around silicone's usual fate of incineration or landfill; the team has filed a patent.

science.headline: NASA's Dragonfly Rotorcraft Completes Its First Simulated Flight Over Titan's Dunes
science.blurb: Engineers ran the most complete test yet of Dragonfly's flight sequence on a Johns Hopkins APL testbed, simulating a flight over Titan-like dunes, a safe-landing-site search and touchdown using real flight software. The craft, launching no earlier than 2028 and arriving at Titan in 2034, must fly itself with no real-time help from Earth.

philosophy.headline: What Physics Can Teach You About Surviving a Messy Life
philosophy.blurb: Zahaan Bharmal, writing after being fired from his first job, argues physics's real value isn't reductionist bragging rights but its models of chaotic systems — which teach that resilience needs surge capacity, and that people tolerate inequality only when a game seems fair. Used humbly, he argues, physics helps us question assumptions and sit with uncertainty.

philosophy.headline: Why Real Peace Requires Rebuilding the Economy, Not Just Signing a Treaty
philosophy.blurb: Azize Aslan argues postwar peace deals routinely fail because they stop direct violence without dismantling the economic structures that fueled the conflict. Drawing on worker cooperatives in Rojava and Colombia's ECOMÚN, she contends lasting peace needs democratically run economies that meet people's needs daily, not a document signed once.

philosophy.headline: Living With Housemates Is Where Your Self-Illusions Go to Die
philosophy.blurb: Elizabeth Oldfield traces today's loneliness epidemic partly to individualism's prizing of privacy and autonomy, arguing from her own household of housemates that being witnessed at our worst by people who stay anyway reshapes character in ways solitude can't. Such communities last, she suggests, only when anchored to a purpose beyond themselves.

philosophy_101.text: A system's reserve ability to absorb a sudden shock without breaking — a concept from physics and engineering that today's essay borrows to describe what makes a person, not just a bridge or a power grid, resilient under stress.

An economy organized around worker- or community-owned enterprises run democratically for collective benefit, rather than investor-owned firms run for profit — the model today's essay on postwar peace points to as more durable than a signed ceasefire.
